headline: Allowed Creed Lounge, 41 Pleasant Street, to stay open until 2:00 a.m. on a three-month trial; approved several one-day liquor and entertainment licenses.
summary: Members approved one-day liquor and entertainment licenses for several events, including events at Institute Park and Green Hill Park. They also approved common victualer and restaurant alcohol licenses, and let Creed Lounge stay open until 2:00 a.m. for a three-month trial. Several applications were postponed to August 20, 2026.
decisions: Approved the July 23, 2026 minutes, 3-0.
Approved one-day liquor and entertainment licenses for HHS-DYO_Casita Cultura Latina at Institute Park, 3-0.
Approved one-day entertainment license for Summer Jam Classic, 59 Quinsigamond Avenue, 3-0.
Postponed the one-day liquor and entertainment applications for Our Lady of Mercy Maronite Catholic Church, 341 June Street, to August 20, 2026, 3-0.
Approved one-day liquor licenses for Christopher Besaw, 280 Main Street, 3-0.
Approved one-day entertainment license for Friendly House Block Party, 36 Wall Street, with amended hours, 3-0.
Approved one-day entertainment license for 2026 Community of Vision Day, Green Hill Park, 3-0.
Approved one-day entertainment license for Fun for a Cause Cornhole Classic, 2 Ionic Avenue, 3-0.
Approved one-day liquor license for J.T. Ethier, 55 Millbrook Street, 3-0.
Approved one-day liquor and entertainment licenses for Noreen Hanlon, 18 Cambridge Street, 3-0.
Approved common victualer license for The Vegan Path, 56 Water Street, 3-0.
Approved common victualer license for Gong Cha Worcester Southbridge LLC, 24 Southbridge Street, 3-0.
Postponed the entertainment license application for Paku Paku, Inc., 215 Chandler Street, to August 20, 2026, 3-0.
Postponed the request for change of manager for Italian American World War Veterans of the US Inc. Post 3, 14 Itam Court, to August 20, 2026, 3-0.
Approved restaurant all alcohol license for Grill and Green Kitchen, Inc., 141 Highland Street, 3-0.
Approved the request to transfer the restaurant all alcohol license from Suveroo LLC to L&D Enterprises LLC, 5 Saugus Place, 3-0. The minutes' vote sentence refers to a one-day liquor license.
Postponed the status hearing for Italian American World War Vets of The US, 14 Itam Court, to August 20, 2026, 3-0.
Voted 3-0 that the video system be installed at Victory Bar and Cigar, LLC, 56 Shrewsbury Street, within 30 days.
Allowed Creed Lounge, 41 Pleasant Street, to stay open until 2:00 a.m. for a trial period of three months, 3-0.
Filed the withdrawal of applicant from Punta Cana, received July 2026.

plain_text:
License Commission 
         Meeting Minutes 
   August 6, 2026 
 
 
Attendance: 
 
Commissioners Present: 
 
 
Anthony Vigliotti, Chair 
Charran Fisher, Commissioner 
Maritza Cruz, Commissioner 
 
Commissioners Absent:  
Staff Present: 
 
 
 
Sgt. Thomas Needham, Worcester Police Department  
Amanda Moran, Law Department 
Deborah Steele, Licensing  
 
 
 Minutes: July 23, 2026 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3- 0 to approve July 23, 2026, License Commission 
minutes. 
 
One Day Liquor & Entertainment Requests 
 
 
1. HHS-DYO_Casita Cultura Latina, Institute Park 
Request for one day liquor license 
Request for one day entertainment license for dancing by patrons, dancing by 
entertainers, live music, amplification system, any other audio or visual show whether 
live or recorded specifically  
• Saturday-October 24, 2026-10:00 a.m. – 4:00 p.m. rain date November 1, 2026 
 
Ana Carolina Villar, participating remotely, stated that this event will be held at Institute Park, and 
they are expecting 1,000 to 2,000 people. They will hire police details for the event, and will use the 
restroom facilities at the park. She stated that the alcohol area will be roped off with one egress and 
exit.
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to approve the one-day liquor and entertainment 
licenses. 
 
List of Exhibits:   
 
Exhibit A:  Application for one day liquor license received and dated July 14, 2026. 
Exhibit B:  Application for one day entertainment license received and dated July 14, 2026. 
 
2. Summer Jam Classic, 59 Quinsigamond Avenue 
Request for one day entertainment license for MC, DJ and musical artists 
• Sunday-August 9, 2026-10:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m. 
 
Anthony Barbosa, participating remotely, stated that this is for annual basketball tournament event. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to approve the one-day entertainment license. 
 
List of Exhibits:  Application for one day entertainment license received and dated July 29, 2026. 
 
3. Our Lady of Mercy Maronite Catholic Church, 341 June Street 
Request for one day liquor license 
Request for one day entertainment license for live music, live show, DJ’s 
• Saturday-September 26, 2026-Noon-11:00 p.m. 
• Sunday-September 27, 2026-11:30 a.m.-6:00 p.m. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to postpone the applications to the August 20, 2026, 
License Commission meeting. 
 
4. Christopher Besaw, 280 Main Street 
Request for one day liquor license 
• Friday, Saturday, August 21, 22, 2026-4:00 p.m.-11:00 p.m.  
 
Christopher Besaw, participating remotely, stated that this will be an additional site for the 
Breakaway Festival and they will have TIPS certified bartenders and have additional security and 
police for event. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to approve the one-day liquor licenses. 
 
List of Exhibits:  Application for one day liquor license received and dated July 27, 2026. 
 
5. Friendly House Block Party, 36 Wall Street 
Request for one day entertainment license for recorded music, DJ 
• Friday-August 21, 2026-3:00 p.m.-5:00 p.m.
Jodi Briggs Pickett appeared upon behalf of the application. She requested to change time of the 
event from 2:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to approve the one-day entertainment license with 
amended hours. 
 
List of Exhibits:  Application for one day entertainment license received and dated July 21, 2026. 
 
6. 2026 Community of Vision Day, Green Hill Park 
Request for one day entertainment license for live music 
• Saturday-October 3, 2026-11:00 a.m.-3:00 p.m.-rain date – October 17, 2026 
 
Harry Ducharme appeared upon behalf of the application. He stated that this is a picnic event to help 
blind children, and they expect around 200 people, and a performer will be playing music. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to approve the one-day entertainment license. 
 
List of Exhibits:  Application for one day entertainment license received and dated July 23, 2026. 
 
7. Fun for a Cause Cornhole Classic, 2 Ionic Avenue 
Request for one day entertainment license for amplification system 
• Saturday-August 22, 2026-10:00 a.m. -4:00 p.m. 
 
Star Winston, participating online, stated that this is for a cornhole event and they are hoping 100-
200 people will attend. She stated that event will take place entirely inside. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to approve the one-day entertainment license. 
 
List of Exhibits:  Application for one day entertainment license received and dated July 21, 2026. 
 
8. J.T. Ethier, 55 Millbrook Street 
Request for one day liquor license  
• Saturday-August 8, 2026-Noon-9:00 p.m.  
 
J.T. Ethier, participating remotely, stated that they are looking to hold an event in the parking lot and 
expect about 300-400 people over course of the day. They will have TIPS certified bartenders. The 
alcohol area will have barriers, and they will have four portable toilets in addition to four indoor 
toilets. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to approve the one-day liquor license. 
 
List of Exhibits:  Application for one day liquor license received and dated July 16, 2026. 
 
9. Noreen Hanlon, 18 Cambridge Street
Request for one day liquor license 
Request for one day entertainment license for radio, music 
• Saturday-August 15, 2026 -11:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. 
 
Matt Hanlon appeared upon behalf of the application. He stated that he looking to have an outdoor 
area as his establishment will be participating in the “Hot Dog Safari” where people travel to 
different establishments by bus for hot dogs. He stated he will be using TIPS certified bartenders and 
will have his own security at the event. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to approve the one-day liquor and entertainment 
licenses. 
 
List of Exhibits:   
 
Exhibit A:  Application for one day liquor license received and dated July 14, 2026. 
Exhibit B:  Application for one day entertainment license received and dated July 14, 2026. 
 
Common Victualer Requests 
 
10. The Vegan Path, 56 Water Street 
Sunday Operating Hours* 
10:00 AM - 03:00 PM 
Monday Operating Hours* 
11:30 AM - 03:30 PM 
Tuesday Operating Hours* 
Closed 
Wednesday Operating Hours* 
Closed 
Thursday Operating Hours* 
11:30 AM - 03:30 PM 
Friday Operating Hours* 
10:00 AM - 03:00 PM; 06:00 PM - 09:00PM 
Saturday Operating Hours* 
10:00 AM - 03:00 PM; 06:00 PM - 09:00PM 
 
Tao Zhou appeared upon behalf of the application. She stated that she is looking to opening a Vegan 
restaurant at the old Queen’s Cup on Water Street. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to approve the common victualer license. 
 
List of Exhibits:  Application for common victualer license received and dated July 21, 2026. 
 
11. Gong Cha Worcester Southbridge LLC, 24 Southbridge Street 
Sunday Operating Hours*
11 am - 9 pm 
Monday Operating Hours* 
11 am - 9 pm 
Tuesday Operating Hours* 
11 am - 9 pm 
Wednesday Operating Hours* 
11 am - 9 pm 
Thursday Operating Hours* 
11 am - 9 pm 
Friday Operating Hours* 
11 am - 9 pm 
Saturday Operating Hours* 
11 am - 9 pm 
 
Wendy Loung, participating remotely, stated that they are looking to do a change of ownership at 
location.  
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to approve the common victualer license. 
 
List of Exhibits:  Application for common victualer license received and dated July 23, 2026. 
 
Alcohol/Entertainment Requests 
 
12. Paku Paku, Inc., 215 Chandler Street 
Request for entertainment license for tv, amplification system, karaoke, DJ 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to postpone the application to the August 20, 2026, 
License Commission meeting. 
 
13. Italian American World War Veterans of the US Inc. Post 3, 14 Itam Court 
Request for change of manager 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to postpone the application to the August 20, 2026, 
License Commission meeting. 
 
14. Grill and Green Kitchen, Inc. 141 Highland Street 
• Request for restaurant all alcohol license  
 
The attorney for the restaurant, participated online, stated that the location is looking to add alcohol 
at the site. 
 
The Commissioners stated that they had viewed the site prior to the meeting.
The hours of operation will be Monday through Friday-11:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m., Saturday-Sunday-11:00 
a.m.-8:00 p.m. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to approve the restaurant all alcohol license. 
 
List of Exhibits:  Application for restaurant all alcohol license received and dated July 22, 2026.  
 
15. L&D Enterprises LLC, 5 Saugus Place, 
• Request for transfer of restaurant all alcohol license from Suveroo LLC  
 
Attorney Hong Tran along with the applicants appeared upon behalf of the application. The hours of 
operation will be Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday 5:00 p.m.-2:00 a.m. 
Closed Tuesday and that also includes the outdoor patio in the hours stated. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to approve the one-day liquor license. 
 
List of Exhibits:  Application for restaurant all alcohol license received and dated April 28, 2026. 
 
Status Hearings 
 
 
16. Italian American World War Vets of The US, 14 Itam Court  
Failure to file amendment paperwork 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to postpone the item to the August 20, 2026, 
License Commission meeting. 
 
17. Victory Bar and Cigar, LLC, 56 Shrewsbury Street 
 
Mark Piscello, owner of the establishment, appeared upon behalf of the item. Sgt. Needham 
reviewed the incident that had occurred and stated that they would like to see video cameras 
installed at establishment.   
 
Mr. Piscillo stated that he already has ordered the camera and hopes to have installed by end of 
week. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 that the video system be installed within 30 days. 
 
 
18. Creed Lounge, 41 Pleasant Street-Request to remove condition and be able to reopen to 
2:00 a.m. 
`
Calvin Paulino, accompanied by Katherine Cruz, represented the establishment. Mr. Paulino 
indicated that there have been no incidents and that most of their clientele do not arrive until 
11:00 p.m. or later. The Commissioners acknowledged that the location has a record of violations; 
however, since the enforcement of the 1:00 a.m. closing time, there have been no incidents. They 
recognized the business implications and expressed their willingness to consider a trial period of 
three months to evaluate the feasibility of extending the closing time to 2:00 a.m. Sgt. Needham 
requested that if the Commission decides to reinstate the 2:00 a.m. closing time, Mr. Paulino, as 
the owner, should be present at the premises during closing to ensure compliance with all 
regulations. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to allow the establishment to stay open until 2:00 
a.m. for a trial period of three months. 
 
Communications 
 
Email: Withdrawal of applicant from Punta Cana received July 2026-Filed 
 
Other Business 
 
Chair Vigliotti asked if staff would survey license holders who stayed open until 3:00 a.m. and get 
feedback.  
 
Adjournment 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to adjourn the meeting at 10:56 a.m.
